description:
HELLO! Welcome to Orbit Analytics! 🚀

We are tackling the Be An Earth System Trend Detective! challenge. We are a passionate team of beginners diving into Earth data analysis and storytelling. While we listed core skills like Data Analysis and Earth Science, you don't need to be an expert to join us! Even with a little prior knowledge or curiosity, you are welcome here. Let's explore our planet together!
summary: I developed Orbit Analytics, an interactive Python and Streamlit web app analyzing 20 years (2005–2025) of NASA MODIS aerosol and GLDAS soil moisture data across four districts in Punjab, Pakistan. Using Mann-Kendall statistical testing, it addresses the challenge by separating seasonal winter smog spikes from true long-term climate trends—helping local planners distinguish short-term air-quality emergencies from multi-decade shifts in agricultural water availability.
details:
What It Does Orbit Analytics lets users explore 20 years (2005–2025) of NASA satellite records across four contrasting districts in Punjab, Pakistan: Gujranwala, Lahore, Multan, and Rawalpindi/Murree.

Key Features

  • Interactive Earth Data Controls: Switch between NASA MODIS-Terra Aerosol Optical Depth (air quality) and NASA GLDAS Root Zone Soil Moisture, adjust the 2005–2025 year slider, and toggle a 12-month de-seasonalized rolling mean.
  • Built-in Statistical Verification: Runs linear regression and the non-parametric Mann-Kendall trend test (significance level 0.05) to prove whether a shift is statistically real or just seasonal noise.
  • 4-District Regional Comparison: Overlays all four districts side-by-side, revealing significant soil moisture gains in Rawalpindi/Murree (+1.4304 kg/m²/yr, p = 0.0032) and Lahore (+0.8489 kg/m²/yr, p = 0.0428), while showing why extreme winter smog swings keep 20-year aerosol p-values above 0.05.
  • Local Action Takeaway: Helps Punjab environmental and agricultural planners separate winter smog emergency response from long-term watershed and irrigation planning.

Tech & Super Intelligence (SI) Disclosure Built with Python, Streamlit, Pandas, SciPy, and Plotly using NASA Giovanni datasets. Super Intelligence (SI) tools assisted with code structuring and editing; all data extraction and analysis were done directly for this challenge.
